stories.h: Court freezes $100m tied to Governors Forum in Paris Club legal fees dispute
stories.e: An Abuja High Court judge has frozen up to $100 million allegedly held by the Nigeria Governors Forum and 29 commercial banks, pending a dispute over unpaid legal fees linked to the Paris Club refund saga. Lawyer Ted Iseghohi-Edwards says he is owed the sum under a 2018 indemnity after acting for local governments in a case that found the federal government liable for $318 million in fees. The matter returns to court on 1 December for arguments on a longer-term injunction.

stories.h: Police declare Nestoil chairman, Sahara Group executive wanted over bank MD threat probe
stories.e: The Nigeria Police Force has declared nine business executives, including Nestoil chairman Ernest Azudialu-Obiejesi and Sahara Group executive director Tope Shonubi, wanted after they failed to appear for questioning. Investigators are probing a parcel containing live ammunition and an explosive device sent to the residence of First Banks managing director in May, which police have linked to disputes over loan recovery from indebted customers. Only one of ten invited executives has so far reported to police.

stories.h: Ozekhome's defence cross-examines CCB official over Useni London property probe
stories.e: In an Abuja trial, lawyers for Mike Ozekhome questioned a Code of Conduct Bureau witness about the investigation into a London property once linked to the late minister Jeremiah Useni. The case centres on allegations that Ozekhome and a co-defendant forged documents to claim ownership of the house after a UK tribunal ruled neither was the rightful owner.

stories.h: INEC names 17,656 polling units for nationwide BVAS mock accreditation exercise
stories.e: Ahead of the 2027 general election, INEC has published a list of 17,656 polling units across all states and the FCT where it will test the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System on 28 November. The exercise is meant to check equipment reliability and accreditation procedures before the real vote.

stories.h: Bayelsa boat tragedy exposes questions over N844m earmarked for boat purchases
stories.e: After a mourners-carrying boat capsized in Bayelsa, killing at least 29 people, scrutiny has turned to N844 million the state budgeted across 2025 and 2026 for marine vessels. Officials have not clarified whether the boats were delivered or where they were deployed, and the Marine and Blue Economy commissioner declined to give immediate answers.

stories.h: SERAP sues INEC and data protection commission over AI-generated photos in voter register
stories.e: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project has filed suit at the Federal High Court in Abuja against the Independent National Electoral Commission and the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, after suspected AI-generated photographs turned up in the preliminary voters register during its October display. The civil society organisation wants the court to order an independent forensic investigation by the data protection commission, rather than leaving the matter to INEC's own internal review, and to establish whether data protection law was breached. INEC had earlier acknowledged flagging hundreds of suspicious entries but maintained that the preliminary register was not yet final.

stories.h: Anti-corruption group demands mandatory accountability checks on government enterprises
stories.e: The Centre for Fiscal Transparency and Public Integrity has urged Nigeria's Fiscal Responsibility Commission to extend its annual assessments to cover revenue-generating parastatals and government-owned enterprises, not just ministries. The group also wants the Fiscal Responsibility Act 2007 amended to let the Commission directly sanction agencies that repeatedly flout financial rules, including withholding their overhead funding.

stories.h: Twenty Kwara correctional officers probed after death-row inmates' escape
stories.e: Two death-row inmates broke out of the Medium Security Custodial Centre in Oke-Kura, Ilorin, before dawn last Wednesday after reportedly spending months digging through a cell wall and scaling the perimeter fence with knotted blankets. The Nigerian Correctional Service has launched a probe, with sources putting the number of officers under investigation, including armed squad members, at about 20, though the Kwara Command says it is too early to confirm a figure.

stories.h: NAFDAC says it destroyed N22.73bn worth of substandard products in eight months
stories.e: Nigeria's drug and food regulator, NAFDAC, says it carried out 22 destruction exercises between January and August 2026 covering unwholesome products worth about N22.73 billion, alongside more than 5,500 enforcement actions, 213 raids and 52 arrests. The agency presented the figures at an international regulators' meeting in Prague, framing them as part of efforts to curb counterfeit goods and retain its World Health Organization maturity rating.

stories.h: Federal Government's domestic borrowing overshoots full-year target by September
stories.e: A new Financial Markets Dealers Association report shows the Federal Government's net domestic borrowing had already reached N20.39 trillion by the end of September, well above the N18.4 trillion ceiling set for the whole of 2026, with a quarter of the fiscal year still to run. The report also found government borrowing growing far faster than credit to the private sector, raising concerns about funding available to businesses even as the central bank trims interest rates.

stories.h: INEC postpones full voter register revalidation ahead of 2027 poll
stories.e: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan has confirmed that a planned six-month revalidation of Nigeria's voters' register, meant to weed out duplicate, underage and deceased entries, cannot be finished before the presidential election set for 16 January 2027. The commission says it will instead keep clearing flagged duplicates and is reconsidering its 15 December deadline for publishing the final register, with a nationwide mock accreditation exercise still planned for 28 November.

stories.h: Analysts warn weak campaign finance oversight threatens economic recovery
stories.e: Economists and governance groups, including the CPPE and PLAC, warn that poorly monitored political spending ahead of the 2027 elections is adding pressure on the naira and could reverse recent gains against inflation. They point to a steep rise in the donor-disclosure threshold under the Electoral Act 2026 as a step that could weaken transparency and deepen elite control of campaign funding.

stories.h: Defence Ministry deletes post on ministers APC rally visit after backlash
stories.e: Nigerias Ministry of Defence removed a social media post describing Defence Minister Christopher Musas inspection of a venue for an All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally, after Nigerians accused him of misusing his office for partisan politics. Critics questioned why a minister responsible for national security was engaged in ruling-party campaign preparations.

stories.h: Press freedom groups warn Cybercrimes Act is being weaponised against journalists
stories.e: Civil society and media groups, including SERAP, Amnesty International Nigeria and the Nigerian Union of Journalists, say security agencies are increasingly using the Cybercrimes Act to arrest and prosecute reporters instead of officials pursuing civil remedies. They cite journalist Daniel Ojukwus continued detention over a report on alleged misuse of public classroom funds as an example of the trend.

stories.h: SERAP sues NDPC, INEC over alleged AI-manipulated voter register
stories.e: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project has taken the National Data Protection Commission and INEC to the Federal High Court in Abuja, alleging that some INEC officials used AI-generated photographs to manipulate the preliminary voters register. SERAP wants the court to compel the NDPC to investigate the claims, examine INECs electronic records for a possible data breach, and use its enforcement powers over any violations of the Nigeria Data Protection Act. INEC has acknowledged flagging hundreds of suspect records ahead of certifying the final register in December.

stories.h: NAFDAC to destroy ₦100bn worth of fake and banned products in Ogun
stories.e: Nigeria's drug and food regulator, NAFDAC, says it will destroy counterfeit and prohibited goods worth an estimated ₦100 billion seized in Ogun State. The exercise forms part of the agency's ongoing crackdown on fake and substandard products circulating in the south-west.

stories.h: Kano council chief dares Amnesty International over "deliver by hook or crook" remark
stories.e: Gwale Local Government Chairman Abubakar Ma'azu Mojo has dismissed Amnesty International's warning that his call for APC supporters to deliver polling units "by hook or by crook" could inflame tension before the 2027 elections. Mojo said the rights group had cherry-picked his remarks while ignoring his record on local development, and dared authorities to arrest him.

stories.h: Delta State targets clearing N6.8bn pension arrears by 2027
stories.e: Delta State's Pension Bureau says it aims to clear N6.8 billion in outstanding pension arrears by 2027, backed by a N10 billion welfare intervention for retirees. Officials told lawmakers during 2027 budget defence that new retirements keep adding to the backlog, even as the state's overall debt has fallen sharply since 2023.

stories.h: Customs suspends training amid Federal Character Commission recruitment row
stories.e: The Nigeria Customs Service has paused training at its two colleges pending consultations with the Federal Character Commission over its 2025 recruitment exercise. The commission is suing the service after more than 500 applicants complained of being excluded from training despite appearing on published shortlists.

stories.h: NAFDAC destroys ₦100bn in fake drugs and cosmetics, uncovers illegal factories
stories.e: Nigeria's drug regulator NAFDAC burned counterfeit, expired and banned medicines, food and cosmetics worth an estimated ₦100 billion at a dumpsite in Ogun State, after raids uncovered a hardware warehouse secretly used to manufacture illegal cosmetics and other sites making fake alcoholic drinks. Director-General Mojisola Adeyeye said those arrested would face prosecution and urged the public to report suspected counterfeit products.

stories.h: Soludo presents N893.44bn Anambra 2027 budget, up 16.58% on this year
stories.e: Anambra Governor Charles Soludo submitted a N893.44 billion budget for 2027 to the state assembly, themed "Solution 2.0: Unlocking New Axis for Sustainable Prosperity." Capital spending takes up more than three-quarters of the plan, with lawmakers welcoming allocations to education, healthcare and agriculture ahead of a promised line-by-line review.

stories.h: IGP warns parties against election violence as 12 parties sign peace pact ahead of 2027
stories.e: Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Disu has warned political parties, candidates and supporters against violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, telling a meeting at Force Headquarters that no political ambition is worth a Nigerian life. Twelve political parties signed a fresh peace agreement committing them to renounce thuggery and settle disputes through the courts, while INECs chairman urged parties to avoid inflammatory rhetoric and the use of private armed security. The commitments follow a string of recent clashes between rival party supporters.

stories.h: ADC demands Tinubus resignation or impeachment over Kano governors Supreme Court claims
stories.e: The African Democratic Congress has called on President Bola Tinubu to resign or face impeachment, after Kano Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf claimed in a BBC Hausa interview that he was sent to negotiate with Tinubu over his pending Supreme Court election case before defecting to the APC. The party wants the National Assembly to investigate the claims and begin impeachment proceedings, though it provided no direct evidence of wrongdoing by Tinubu. The Kwankwasiyya Movement has denied sending Yusuf on any such mission.

stories.h: Court nullifies Omo-Ageges NDC Senate nomination, leaving party no time for fresh primary
stories.e: A Federal High Court in Warri has nullified Ovie Omo-Ageges nomination as the NDCs candidate for Delta Central senatorial district in the 2027 elections, ordering INEC to delist him. Justice Hyeladzira Nganjiwa ruled that the NDC failed to submit its membership register on time and that Omo-Agege was still registered with the APC when the NDCs primary took place. The court held that the statutory deadline for the party to conduct a fresh primary has already passed.

stories.h: NEC backs $350m World Bank-supported disaster preparedness programme
stories.e: Nigeria's National Economic Council has endorsed a six-year, $350 million World Bank-backed scheme called ARISE-Nigeria, aimed at improving the country's response to floods, droughts and fires. Vice President Kashim Shettima, who chaired the meeting, said the programme would strengthen early warning systems and emergency operations centres, starting in five to ten states.

stories.h: NEC approves extra N130bn for police training institutions, taking total to N230bn
stories.e: Nigeria's National Economic Council has approved an additional N130 billion to renovate police training colleges, raising total committed funding to N230 billion. Work is under way at 13 locations and is roughly 30 per cent complete, with the council hoping to speed up rehabilitation ahead of a planned recruitment of 50,000 new police personnel.

stories.h: Opposition unity under strain as Atiku, Obi and Makinde weigh rival 2027 ambitions
stories.e: With just over a year to the 2027 polls, analysts say the personal ambitions of Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi and Seyi Makinde are complicating efforts to build a single opposition front against the ruling party. Each retains a distinct support base, making a merger of their followings far from straightforward.

stories.h: Kano governor says estranged wife was taken from Government House amid divorce filing
stories.e: Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf has publicly discussed the breakdown of his marriage to Zainab Kwankwaso, telling BBC Hausa she left Government House and later filed for divorce without his knowledge. He linked the rift to his political fallout with her guardian, former governor Rabiu Kwankwaso, after he defected from the NNPP to the APC.

stories.h: Atiku denies quitting 2027 race after support group's defection to Obi
stories.e: The Coalition of Atiku Support Groups Initiative announced it was switching its backing to Peter Obi's Nigeria Democratic Congress ticket, citing the case for power rotation and opposition unity, prompting reports that Atiku had stepped down. Atiku's campaign rejected this, insisting no group could withdraw him from the race and accusing those spreading the claim of serving President Tinubu's interests.

stories.h: Atiku dismisses claim he withdrew from 2027 presidential race as a 'brazen falsehood'
stories.e: Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has denied reports that he stepped down from the 2027 presidential contest, with his spokesman Phrank Shaibu describing the claim as a deliberate falsehood designed to clear the field for President Bola Tinubu. Atiku insists he remains in the race and that the matter will be settled by voters at the ballot box on 16 January 2027.

stories.h: APC headquarters mediates Akume-Alia power struggle in Benue
stories.e: The ruling All Progressives Congress convened a reconciliation meeting in Abuja between Benue Governor Hyacinth Alia and the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, whose rival factions have each installed their own state party executives. Alia has linked the dispute to his refusal to share state funds with some party figures ahead of the 2027 elections.

stories.h: Jonathan warns self-interested politics is holding Nigeria back
stories.e: Former President Goodluck Jonathan told an Abuja colloquium on Nigerias global image that politicians chasing personal gain, rather than their parties policies, are dragging the country backwards. He urged leaders to invest in young people and institutions rather than personal wealth, pointing to corruption, insecurity and weak institutions as reasons for Nigerias declining international reputation. Jonathan called for reforms to make political recruitment and elections more merit-based and transparent.

stories.h: Adeola, Adebutu, Lawal emerge frontrunners in race to succeed Abiodun in Ogun
stories.e: Three candidates have emerged as frontrunners to succeed Governor Dapo Abiodun in Ogun State's 2027 governorship race: the APC's Senator Solomon Adeola, the PDP's Ladi Adebutu, who narrowly lost to Abiodun in 2023, and the ADC's Jimi Lawal. Zoning, party unity and Ogun West's long wait for a governor loom large over the contest.

stories.h: Tinubu pledges to halve out-of-school children, hire 20,000 teachers by 2031
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu has promised that his administration will cut the number of out-of-school children in Nigeria by half and recruit 20,000 additional teachers within the next five years, as part of a renewed education push ahead of the 2027 elections.

stories.h: Tinubu promises improved electricity supply at Oyo campaign rally
stories.e: Campaigning in Oyo State, President Bola Tinubu told supporters he guarantees improvements to Nigerias electricity supply, reviving a pledge first made during his 2023 campaign that opposition figures, including Oyo Governor Seyi Makinde, have accused him of failing to keep. The renewed promise comes as rival candidates make their own power-sector commitments ahead of the 2027 election.

stories.h: Federal High Court rules on ADC eligibility suit against Tinubu and Adamawa ticket dispute
stories.e: A Federal High Court judge in Abuja refused to let the African Democratic Congress amend its suit challenging President Bola Tinubus eligibility for 2027, ruling the case must proceed on its original filing. In a separate judgment, another judge ordered the ADC to reinstate Omar Suleiman as its Adamawa governorship candidate and barred INEC from recognising a rival nominee. Meanwhile, ADC presidential candidate Peter Obi pledged 10,000 megawatts of electricity if elected, part of a wider slate of infrastructure promises for which he gave no timetable.

stories.h: Makinde criticises Fashola over defence of Tinubus electricity promise
stories.e: Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde has criticised former works minister Babatunde Fashola for defending President Tinubus 2023 pledge to fix Nigerias electricity supply, which Makinde says remains unmet. The exchange is part of an ongoing political dispute over whether Tinubu has delivered on his campaign commitment to end unreliable power supply.

stories.h: Court orders ADC to drop Ribadu, restore Suleiman as Adamawa candidate
stories.e: A Federal High Court in Abuja ruled that the ADC's national leadership had no lawful basis to replace Omar Suleiman, winner of the party's Adamawa governorship primary, with Tukur Ribadu, and ordered INEC to restore Suleiman as the candidate. The judge found Suleiman had filed his challenge within the required 14-day window, while Ribadu had never successfully contested the primary result through the party's internal appeal process.

stories.h: Police invite Edo council chairman after armed attack on NDC secretariat
stories.e: Edo State Police have invited Owan East Local Government Chairman Ernest Oyaole Aitalegbe for questioning after armed men allegedly stormed the National Democratic Congress secretariat in Afuze, destroying campaign materials and threatening occupants. NDC senatorial candidate Mariam Iseme and Professor Grant Eruhagan said the attackers wore uniforms resembling those of the Edo State Security Network. Police Commissioner Patrick Daaor warned that anyone sponsoring political violence would be prosecuted.

stories.h: ADC questions Tinubu's reliance on World Bank over fuel subsidy removal
stories.e: African Democratic Congress spokesperson Bolaji Abdullahi has accused President Tinubu's administration of prioritising World Bank recommendations over the welfare of Nigerians in removing the petrol subsidy, arguing the institution was never elected to govern the country. He cited rising public debt and debt-servicing costs, and urged government to cut spending on aircraft, yachts and convoys before asking citizens to endure further hardship.

stories.h: SEC approves Dangote Refinery IPO share allotment after N5.85 trillion subscription rush
stories.e: Nigerias Securities and Exchange Commission has approved the share allotment for Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals initial public offering, after subscriptions reached about N5.85 trillion, nearly three times the original offer size. Investors are set to receive 5.196 billion shares, with Aliko Dangote retaining roughly 84 per cent ownership, and trading on the Nigerian Exchange is expected to begin on 8 December. The offer, originally priced at N525 per share, was oversubscribed enough to trigger the option to enlarge it by up to 30 per cent.

stories.h: Finance minister admits economic gains yet to reach most households
stories.e: Coordinating Minister of the Economy Taiwo Oyedele has acknowledged that while macroeconomic indicators are improving, ordinary households and businesses are still waiting to feel meaningful relief. His comments echo growing criticism from economists that stabilisation on paper has not yet translated into cheaper food, transport or better business conditions for most Nigerians.

stories.h: Power minister warns Nigerians may wait three to five years for reliable electricity
stories.e: Power Minister Joseph Tegbe has said significant improvement in Nigeria's electricity supply could take another three to five years, blaming decades of neglected infrastructure and poor past investment decisions. He ruled out a near-term tariff rise and said the government had renegotiated its debt to power generation companies from N6 trillion down to N3.3 trillion, of which N1.23 trillion has been paid.

stories.h: Domestic investors drive NGX equity turnover to record N17.13trn in ten months
stories.e: Nigerian Exchange data for January to October 2026 shows equity turnover rose 79% year-on-year to N17.13 trillion, with local institutional and retail investors supplying over 90% of trading as foreign participation shrank to under 10%. Market capitalisation closed October at a record N165.11 trillion.

stories.h: Food inflation tops 20% in 19 Nigerian states even as national rate eases
stories.e: NBS figures for October show annual food inflation easing slightly nationwide to 19.13%, yet 19 states still recorded rates above 20%, with Ondo, Lagos and Imo worst affected. Analysts warn prices could climb again as the harvest season ends and transport costs rise.

stories.h: Cooking gas prices climb again in Abuja as residents ration supplies
stories.e: Liquefied petroleum gas now sells for between ₦1,600 and ₦2,000 per kilogram across the Federal Capital Territory, up from October's range, with residents in areas such as Gudu, Lugbe and Karu reporting they are buying smaller quantities or switching to charcoal. Industry sources and the NMDPRA blame supply disruptions, high logistics costs, foreign exchange volatility and distribution bottlenecks for the latest increase.

stories.h: Tinubu campaign council says ₦450bn agricultural financing has reached 500,000 farmers
stories.e: The APC Presidential Campaign Council says federal agricultural financing programmes worth ₦450 billion have reached more than 500,000 smallholder farmers across 16 states, part of a wider push that includes a separate fertiliser initiative targeting two million farmers. The figures, released as a campaign statement, are intended to showcase the administration's food security record ahead of the 2027 election.

stories.h: Economist Rewane projects Nigeria's capital market could more than double to N519.75trn by 2028
stories.e: Speaking at the 2026 Parthian Economic Discourse in Lagos, economist Bismarck Rewane forecast that Nigeria's capital market could grow 2.25 times to reach N519.75 trillion by 2028, driven by new listings, stronger domestic investor participation and ongoing reforms. He also projected inflation could fall to around 13 per cent by 2028, while cautioning that lasting progress requires institutional reform rather than policy changes alone.

stories.h: Listed firms combined tax bill jumps 72% to N4.6 trillion under new tax reforms
stories.e: Thirty companies on the Nigerian Exchange paid an estimated N4.6 trillion in taxes in the first nine months of 2026, up 72 per cent, after the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 consolidated several levies into a single development levy. Analysts say the sharply higher tax bills, led by oil, telecoms and cement firms, could squeeze shareholder returns and invite closer scrutiny of corporate tax compliance.

stories.h: Nigerias wet-season harvest set to ease food prices if bottlenecks are fixed
stories.e: A new survey by Ahmadu Bello Universitys agricultural extension service projects higher output for 13 of 17 major crops this season, with cereal production up nearly 2 per cent. Researchers warn that poor storage, high transport costs, flooding and insecurity could stop these gains from reaching consumers plates.

stories.h: Naira nears N1,400/$ as external reserves drop $610m in under a month
stories.e: The naira weakened to N1,389.73 per dollar on the official market, edging closer to N1,400, as Nigerias external reserves fell by roughly $610 million in under a month to $54.65 billion by 19 November. Analysts linked the pressure to tight FX supply, election-related uncertainty and rising festive-season dollar demand, despite increased Central Bank dollar sales.

stories.h: Dangote, Otedola and four other billionaires lose ₦2.19trn in a week
stories.e: The tracked stock-market holdings of six of Nigeria's wealthiest businessmen, including Aliko Dangote and Femi Otedola, fell by an estimated ₦2.19 trillion in the week to 20 November as the Nigerian Exchange's All-Share Index dropped by about 2 per cent. Dangote accounted for most of the decline, losing roughly ₦2.08 trillion as Dangote Cement shares fell nearly 10 per cent, while a Friday sell-off also wiped billions off major bank stocks.

stories.h: Dangote refinery cuts petrol price to four-month low amid naira-linked pricing
stories.e: The Dangote Petroleum Refinery has reduced its ex-depot petrol price to N1,070 per litre, its lowest level since July, after returning to a pricing model linked to international benchmark EBOB. The cut follows a volatile month in which prices briefly rose above N1,300 under a fixed-naira arrangement before falling back through roughly six reductions. Whether motorists see lower pump prices will depend on how marketers and distributors pass on the reduction.

stories.h: Nigeria's diesel imports jump 917% in October as domestic demand rises
stories.e: Nigeria's diesel imports surged by 917 per cent in October compared with September, according to the latest NMDPRA factsheet, even as local refineries also increased output. Total diesel supply rose 93 per cent to 16.8 million litres a day, though stock cover fell to just under 44 days from nearly 50. The regulator's figures suggest the country's fuel security still depends heavily on imports despite growing local refining capacity.

stories.h: Joblessness drives over a quarter of new Nigerian businesses in 2026 - report
stories.e: The Fate Institute's State of Entrepreneurship report, unveiled in Lagos, found that 26.5 per cent of new businesses launched in 2026 were started mainly because founders could not find jobs rather than to pursue a specific opportunity. The report found overall business growth rose to 75 per cent from 67 per cent a year earlier, while persistent power shortages and skill gaps continue to limit productivity.

stories.h: FG domestic borrowing hits 110% of 2026 annual target by September
stories.e: A report by the Financial Markets Dealers Association shows the Federal Government's net domestic borrowing reached N20.32 trillion by the end of September 2026, about N1.92 trillion above the N18.4 trillion target set for the whole year in the 2026 budget. The report also found domestic debt-service payments rose roughly 21 per cent quarter-on-quarter to about N2.6 trillion, as total public debt stood at N166.79 trillion as of June 2026.

stories.h: Otti presents N1.2trn 2027 budget to Abia Assembly
stories.e: Abia State Governor Alex Otti has presented a N1.2 trillion appropriation bill for 2027 to the state House of Assembly, an 18 per cent rise on the current year's budget, with about 80 per cent earmarked for capital projects. The governor said roughly N552.67 billion of the budget would be funded through concessional loans, while lawmakers promised a line-by-line review before passage.

stories.h: Nigerian stocks lose N3 trillion in three days as Dangote Cement, Aradel and banks tumble
stories.e: The Nigerian Exchange's All-Share Index fell from a record 254,763 points to 248,286 points over three sessions, with Dangote Cement down nearly 10 per cent and Aradel Holdings hitting its daily trading limit. Analysts attributed the slide to profit-taking, investors freeing up cash ahead of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery's planned listing, falling oil prices and a weakening naira.

stories.h: Abia governor presents N1.2trn budget for 2027
stories.e: Governor Alex Otti has presented a N1.2 trillion appropriation bill for 2027 to the Abia State House of Assembly, an 18 per cent rise on this years budget. About 80 per cent is earmarked for capital projects, with education and healthcare taking the largest shares of planned social spending, while over N552 billion is expected to come from concessional loans tied to infrastructure.

stories.h: FG to roll over unspent 2026 capital budget into 2027
stories.e: The Federal Ministry of Finance says it will carry forward unspent 2026 capital spending into the 2027 budget, moving towards a single annual budget cycle. Coordinating Minister of the Economy Taiwo Oyedele announced the plan after an Economic Management Team meeting in Abuja, which also reviewed the 2027 Finance Bill and a 90-day plan to stabilise food prices.

stories.h: Naira steady at N1,450 as CBN opens $1m cash window for BDCs
stories.e: The naira held firm at N1,450 to the dollar on the parallel market on Wednesday after the Central Bank of Nigeria authorised bureau de change operators to access a $1 million cash window, a move aimed at narrowing the gap between official and street exchange rates and easing dollar liquidity pressure.

stories.h: Nigeria's foreign reserves slip back to early-September levels as FX liquidity tightens
stories.e: Nigeria's gross external reserves have retreated to levels last seen in early September, erasing roughly two months of earlier gains, as heavy foreign exchange drawdowns in November put renewed pressure on the central bank's buffers. The decline comes despite recent CBN efforts to stabilise the naira and boost dollar liquidity.

stories.h: CBN reaffirms single-digit inflation target, promises policy consistency into 2027
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria has signalled it will hold its current monetary policy direction steady going into 2027, reaffirming its long-term goal of bringing inflation down to single digits. The bank described its outlook for the coming year as cautious, pointing to ongoing efforts to stabilise prices and the naira.

stories.h: CBN holds benchmark rate at 23% as inflation eases to 14.06% in October
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigerias Monetary Policy Committee has unanimously voted to hold its benchmark interest rate at 23 per cent, alongside unchanged cash reserve requirements, after headline inflation eased to 14.06 per cent in October from 14.63 per cent in September according to the National Bureau of Statistics. Analysts cautioned that the disinflation trend may not be strong enough to justify a rate cut, warning that pre-election government spending and rising energy costs could reignite price pressures in the run-up to the 2027 polls.

stories.h: Twelve Nigerian banks grow combined assets to N253trn in nine months
stories.e: Twelve deposit money banks reported combined total assets of N253 trillion for the nine months to September 2026, about 7 per cent higher than a year earlier, driven by increased lending and customer deposits. Access Holdings remained the largest lender by assets, while Ecobank's Nigerian assets fell, and analysts noted some smaller banks' rapid growth was partly linked to investments in government securities.

stories.h: CBN governor presses for bigger Nigerian role in planned ECOWAS Monetary Union
stories.e: Central Bank of Nigeria Governor Olayemi Cardoso has called for Nigeria to be given a proportionally larger say in the governance of the planned ECOWAS Monetary Union, arguing that larger economies carrying more financial risk should have a correspondingly bigger role. He spoke at a three-day Abidjan meeting preparing for the phased rollout of the regional ECO currency from 2027.

stories.h: FCMB Group's nine-month pretax profit more than doubles to ₦272.8bn
stories.e: FCMB Group reported a 103 per cent rise in pretax profit to ₦272.8 billion for the nine months to September 2026, with gross earnings up 21 per cent to ₦1 trillion and its cost-to-income ratio improving sharply. Chief executive Ladi Balogun said he now expects full-year return on equity to beat the bank's earlier 25 per cent guidance.

stories.h: Stanbic IBTCs profit surge raises questions over earnings sustainability
stories.e: Stanbic IBTCs profit after tax rose 33 per cent to N370.4 billion in the first nine months of 2026, driven largely by a huge jump in trading income. Analysts at CardinalStone caution that the trading gains reflect one-off market volatility rather than a sustainable new earnings base, and forecast a sharp fall in trading revenue once yields stabilise.

stories.h: UBA's nine-month pre-tax profit falls 13% to N503bn on higher loan impairments
stories.e: United Bank for Africa reported a 13.1 per cent drop in pre-tax profit to N502.98 billion for the nine months to September 2026, as credit impairment charges nearly quintupled to N272.12 billion. Gross earnings and operating income still grew, lifted by stronger foreign exchange and non-interest income, while the bank's balance sheet continued to expand with total assets up 5.4 per cent to N34.96 trillion.

stories.h: Naira nears N1,400/$ as external reserves shed $610m in under a month
stories.e: Nigeria's naira weakened to N1,389.73 to the dollar on the official market, edging closer to the N1,400 mark, as external reserves fell by about $610 million since late October to $54.65 billion. Analysts blamed tight forex supply, election-related capital outflows and seasonal festive demand for the pressure.

stories.h: Niger State-backed firm opens N70 billion bond at 24 per cent to fund infrastructure
stories.e: North Central Nigeria Investment Plc, sponsored by the Niger State government, has opened a N70 billion bond offer paying 24 per cent annually, with repayments funded through monthly deductions from the states federal allocation. Proceeds are earmarked for roads and healthcare infrastructure, but the arrangement carries no federal guarantee, leaving repayment dependent on the state continuing to receive sufficient allocations.

stories.h: Naira slides to ₦1,400/$ despite CBN selling $1.3bn to defend it
stories.e: The naira weakened 2.5 per cent to close at ₦1,394/$ on Friday after touching ₦1,400 intraday, extending a fifth straight day of losses even though the Central Bank sold about $1.3 billion to meet surging dollar demand. Analysts linked the pressure to festive-season import demand, weaker foreign inflows and investor caution ahead of Nigeria's 2027 elections, with the CBN's rate-setting committee due to meet on 23 and 24 November.

stories.h: FCMB Groups nine-month profit jumps 86% on stronger interest income
stories.e: FCMB Group reported an 86 per cent year-on-year rise in net profit for the nine months to September, with revenue up 21 per cent to around N1 trillion. Net interest income climbed as funding costs eased, and profit before tax more than doubled, prompting the banks chief executive to forecast stronger full-year returns.

stories.h: FCMB's nine-month pre-tax profit more than doubles to ₦272.8bn
stories.e: FCMB Group reported a 103 per cent rise in pre-tax profit to ₦272.8 billion for the nine months to September 2026, driven by higher net interest income and cheaper deposits, and beating its own third-quarter forecast. The bank's non-performing loan ratio also rose, to 6.4 per cent, after a second-quarter clean-up of its loan book pushed impairment charges higher.

stories.h: Nigeria's payment system retains status as Africa's only 'mature' system - report
stories.e: The AfricaNenda Foundation's 2026 State of Inclusive Instant Payment Systems report found Nigeria's National Instant Payment system remains the only one on the continent rated 'mature', a status it has held since 2025. The report credited the system's identity verification and consumer recourse mechanisms, while warning of rising payment fraud across Africa more broadly.

stories.h: FCMB Group doubles nine-month profit to N272.8bn on margin growth
stories.e: FCMB Group's profit before tax more than doubled to N272.8 billion for the nine months to September 2026, driven by stronger net interest margins and digital revenue growth. Profit after tax rose to N232.9 billion, lifting the lender's nine-month return on equity to 30 per cent, with the chief executive signalling full-year returns could exceed earlier guidance.

stories.h: Naira slips to eight-month low against the dollar
stories.e: The naira closed at N1,388 to the dollar on Thursday, its weakest level since early March, as official exchange-rate data from the Central Bank showed a further slide to N1,376.58. Interbank foreign exchange turnover jumped by nearly 60 per cent from the previous day, reflecting a sharp rise in dollar demand this week.

stories.h: Tax authority sets 30 November deadline for crypto operators to register
stories.e: The Nigeria Revenue Service has ordered individuals and businesses engaged in virtual asset activities to register on its newly launched Virtual Asset Service Provider Tax Portal by 30 November, with full technical integration due by 31 December. The agency says the move, backed by the 2025 Nigeria Tax Administration Act, is meant to strengthen tax compliance and support anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorism-financing checks across crypto exchanges, custodians and payment platforms operating in or serving Nigeria.

stories.h: CBN, NNPC sign deal to tighten oil revenue oversight, boost forex inflows
stories.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria and state oil firm NNPC have signed a memorandum of understanding aimed at tightening oversight of oil and gas revenue and channelling more foreign exchange through official channels. Under the agreement, NNPC will align its domestic payments and contractor settlements with CBN rules, while the central bank sets up a dedicated unit to manage the oil firms transactions and support the naira stability.

stories.h: Naira weakens to N1,379.99/$ as interbank FX turnover tops $500 million
stories.e: The naira depreciated to N1,379.99 against the US dollar as interbank foreign exchange turnover exceeded $500 million in a single trading session. The movement highlights continuing volatility in Nigeria's market-driven exchange rate regime.

stories.h: Dangote Refinery eyes 1 December for historic N65.2trn NGX listing
stories.e: Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals is targeting as early as 1 December to begin trading on the Nigerian Exchange, in a debut valued at about N65.2 trillion. The listing, pending final regulatory clearance, would mark one of the largest in NGX history and significantly expand the exchange's market capitalisation.

stories.h: Diesel imports surge tenfold as Dangote refinery exports bulk of its output
stories.e: Nigeria's diesel imports jumped more than tenfold in October after the Dangote refinery shipped over half of its production abroad, pushing local marketers back toward imported supply. The trend highlights how export decisions by the country's dominant refiner can still leave the domestic market exposed.

stories.h: Federal Government partners US firm Valmont to build irrigation equipment factory in Nigeria
stories.e: Nigeria's Presidential Implementation Committee on Technology Transfer has signed an agreement with US firm Valmont Industries, the world's largest maker of centre-pivot irrigation systems, to set up local manufacturing and transfer technology for mechanised irrigation. The deal, tied to the wider Irrigate Nigeria Programme and a planned 40,000-hectare pilot scheme in Adamawa State, aims to cut reliance on imported irrigation equipment in a country where only about 5.8 per cent of farmland is currently irrigated.

stories.h: Rising costs squeeze Nigeria's palm oil producers despite import boom
stories.e: Nigeria's leading palm oil producers, Presco and Okomu, are facing shrinking profits as production costs climb faster than revenue, even as the country's import bill for crude palm oil surged nearly sixfold in the first half of 2026. Industry figures say Nigeria still faces a structural supply deficit and warn that importation alone will not solve it.

stories.h: Dangote refinery raises petrol supply 12 per cent as fuel imports jump 47 per cent
stories.e: The Dangote refinery increased its domestic petrol supply by 12 per cent to 31.89 million litres a day in October, even as petrol imports into Nigeria rose 47 per cent to 15 million litres daily, according to official downstream regulator data. Petrol stock cover fell to 21.8 days, below the regulators 30-day benchmark, pointing to continued reliance on imports despite the refinery running above its installed capacity.

stories.h: Nigeria breaks ground on local passport factory for six million booklets
stories.e: Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo broke ground on a National Passport Manufacturing Centre in Abuja designed to produce six million passport booklets a year, expandable to ten million, well above Nigeria's roughly two-million-booklet domestic demand. The minister said the AI-driven, off-grid facility, expected to be completed by May 2027, could eventually supply passport booklets to neighbouring countries too.

stories.h: Nigeria breaks ground on $70m passport booklet factory in Abuja
stories.e: Construction has begun on a $70 million passport booklet factory at the Nigeria Immigration Service headquarters in Abuja, financed through a private-sector partnership with IRIS Smart Technologies rather than direct federal funding. The plant is designed to produce six million electronic passport booklets a year, well above Nigeria's estimated annual demand, with surplus capacity earmarked for other markets. Local production is targeted to begin by May 2027, when President Bola Tinubu is expected to commission the facility.

stories.h: Grid operator warns steel and cement firms over power-quality violations
stories.e: The Nigerian Independent System Operator has directed steel and cement manufacturers connected to the national grid to curb harmonic distortion from furnaces and other equipment or face regulatory sanctions. NISO's management said unchecked interference is straining the grid, overheating equipment and degrading power quality for other users, and set out five compliance steps including power-quality audits and harmonic-mitigation technology. The directive follows a stakeholder engagement in Abuja involving the NERC, TCN and NEMSA.

stories.h: Yutong to build CNG bus assembly plant in Ibadan under federal transport initiative
stories.e: Chinese bus maker Yutong, the world's largest by sales volume, is to establish a compressed natural gas bus assembly plant in Ibadan in partnership with the Presidential Initiative on CNG and Electric Vehicles. The deal, which supports a federal programme aiming to cut transport fares by about 40 per cent on participating routes, will see an initial batch of 300 buses supplied, with the first 100 reaching Lagos by the end of December 2026.

stories.h: Chinese bus giant Yutong to build CNG assembly plant in Ibadan
stories.e: Yutong, described as the worlds largest bus manufacturer, has agreed to set up a compressed natural gas bus assembly plant at the former Leyland Automotive site in Ibadan, under Nigerias Presidential Initiative on CNG and Electric Vehicles. The firm will initially supply 300 CNG buses, with the first 100 expected in Lagos by December, as part of a push to cut transport fares by around 40 per cent on participating routes.

stories.h: Nigerian drugmakers raise factory investment 81% to N29.26bn
stories.e: Nigeria's five listed pharmaceutical manufacturers increased capital spending by 81 per cent to about N29.26 billion in the first nine months of 2026, channelling the funds into factories and machinery to expand local production capacity. The rise reflects a broader push by domestic drugmakers to scale up manufacturing rather than rely on imports.

stories.h: Dangote Sinotruk unveils first locally assembled electric trucks in Africa
stories.e: Dangote Sinotruk West Africa, a joint venture between Dangote Group and China's Sinotruk, has rolled out what it calls the first new-energy commercial trucks assembled on the African continent, at a ceremony in Lagos. Sinotruk's president hailed the launch as a milestone for Nigeria's automotive manufacturing and its shift towards cleaner transport, though the firm says real savings will depend on charging infrastructure and electricity costs.

stories.h: Dangote Sinotruk unveils Nigeria's first locally assembled electric truck
stories.e: Dangote Sinotruk West Africa rolled out what it calls Nigeria's first locally assembled electric heavy-duty truck at its Lagos plant, following the joint venture's earlier move into CNG-powered vehicles. Executives from Dangote and Sinotruk said wider adoption will depend on building charging infrastructure and training local technicians.

stories.h: AKK gas pipeline nears completion as Kano firm protests land seizure
stories.e: NNPC says the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano gas pipeline mainline is about 95 per cent complete, with gas due in Abuja before year-end and in Kaduna and Kano by 2027. A Kano manufacturer, A.B. Janruwa Enterprises, says over four hectares of its land were taken for the project's development corridor without formal notice or compensation, a claim the state government disputes.

stories.h: Regulator flags 13 high-risk oil wells in Rivers gas seepage probe
stories.e: The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission says 13 of 28 oil and gas wells it screened near a gas seepage site in Bille community, Rivers State, are high risk, with inspectors finding active gas leaks, corrosion and vandalism at several facilities. The regulator is now running geochemical tests to trace the source of the emissions and has warned that residents may need to be evacuated if the seepage turns out to be a natural geological event.

stories.h: Nigerian drugmakers raise factory investment 81% to N29.26bn
stories.e: Nigeria's five listed pharmaceutical manufacturers lifted combined capital spending by 81 per cent to N29.26 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up from N16.20 billion a year earlier, as they expand local production capacity. MeCure Industries and Fidson Healthcare accounted for the largest share of the new spending, while combined revenue across the five firms grew 17.2 per cent to N220.27 billion. The investment drive is being driven partly by government efforts to boost domestic drug manufacturing and by the exit of multinational firms such as GSK from the market.

stories.h: NUPRC approves 595 well re-entries and 145 new drilling operations as rig count hits 100
stories.e: Nigeria's upstream petroleum regulator, the NUPRC, said it has approved 595 well re-entries and 145 new drilling operations, pushing the country's active rig count to 100 for the first time in years. The commission described the increase as evidence of renewed investor confidence in Nigeria's oil and gas sector following recent reforms. A higher rig count typically signals increased future production and could support government revenue projections tied to oil output.

stories.h: Nigerian industrial goods firms' tax payments surge 99% under new tax law
stories.e: Seven listed Nigerian industrial goods companies, including Dangote Cement, BUA Cement and Beta Glass, paid a combined N271.7 billion in income tax in the first nine months of 2026, almost double the same period last year, as Nigeria's new tax framework took effect from January 2026. Combined pre-tax profit across the group rose 43 per cent to N2.49 trillion, though Dangote Cement's own tax bill fell even as its profit grew.

stories.h: Nigeria to start local production of pharmaceutical ingredients by Q1 2027, FG says
stories.e: The Federal Government says Nigeria will begin manufacturing active pharmaceutical ingredients locally from the first quarter of 2027, with a major pharmaceutical company set to build the production plant. PVAC National Coordinator Mukhtar Abdul announced the plan at the 2026 Joint Annual Review in Abuja, framing it as a move to cut reliance on imports. A 2026 KPMG report found that roughly nine in ten active ingredients and excipients used by Nigerian drug makers are currently imported.

stories.h: Nigerian Breweries, Nestle Nigeria and peers book N129.4bn in fees to foreign parents
stories.e: Nigerian Breweries, Nestle Nigeria and several other consumer goods manufacturers paid a combined N129.4 billion in fees and royalties to their foreign parent companies, according to newly reviewed financial filings. The figures renew questions about how much value locally listed manufacturers retain domestically versus what flows abroad.

stories.h: Six killed in Delta as gunmen attack NDC campaign tour, including activist and ex-lawmaker
stories.e: Armed men killed six people, among them former Delta lawmaker Moses Anaughe and youth rights activist Efemena Umukoro, during an attack on a campaign tour by NDC senatorial candidate Ovie Omo-Agege in Uduere community, Ughelli North. The victim's family has alleged involvement by aides to the state governor, a claim police say remains under investigation, while the killing has sparked protests demanding justice.

stories.h: Katsina suspends Emir of Dauras official engagements over tourists sexual assault allegation
stories.e: The Katsina State Government has suspended all official engagements and travel for the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, after a foreign tourist alleged he touched her without consent during a palace visit on 14 November. Governor Dikko Radda has set up a committee to investigate the allegation, which the tourist says she partly recorded, though the circulated footage does not conclusively confirm the claim. The state has not said whether the emir faces suspension from the throne itself.

stories.h: Rights groups demand probe after tourist accuses Emir of Daura of sexual assault
stories.e: A foreign tourist has alleged that the 92-year-old Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar-Faruk, touched her inappropriately during a palace visit on 14 November, and posted video of the encounter online after leaving Nigeria. Amnesty International Nigeria has called on Katsina State authorities and police to investigate independently and transparently, while the emirate says it is reviewing the footage and police say they have received no formal complaint.

stories.h: Court told suspected IPOB members gave statements to SSS voluntarily
stories.e: During the trial of four suspected IPOB members accused of killing a security operative, a defence lawyer told an Abuja federal court that the defendants' statements to the SSS were obtained voluntarily, with a Legal Aid Council lawyer present. The case is being watched alongside the separate, higher-profile trial of IPOB leader Nnamdi Kanu over similar questions about how confessional statements were obtained.

stories.h: Scores reported killed in reprisal attacks after bandits murder Niger village head
stories.e: A herders' association says around 64 Fulani residents were killed in Borgu LGA after vigilantes retaliated for a bandit attack that killed a village head, his wife and three children. The toll is unverified by police or the state government, which says joint security teams have been deployed to the area.

stories.h: Calls grow for suspension of Emir of Daura over tourist's sexual assault allegation
stories.e: A viral video said to show the Emir of Daura making unwanted sexual advances on a foreign tourist has prompted former military governor Abubakar Dangiwa Umar and cleric Ahmad Gumi to demand his suspension pending investigation. The footage has not been independently authenticated, and neither the emirate nor the authorities have announced findings.

stories.h: Bandits abduct 13, including baby, in Zamfara as police arrest gunrunner in Niger State
stories.e: Armed bandits raided Jabaka village in Zamfara State's Maru Local Government Area, abducting thirteen residents including an eleven-month-old baby, and police have launched a manhunt for the attackers. In a related operation reported the same day, police in Borgu, Niger State, arrested a suspect accused of supplying locally fabricated AK-47 rifles to armed groups active in the region. The twin incidents underline the persistent insecurity in parts of north-western Nigeria despite ongoing security operations.

stories.h: Amnesty International demands probe into sexual assault allegation against Daura Emir
stories.e: A foreign tourist has accused the Emir of Daura, Faruk Umar Faruk, of touching her inappropriately during a palace visit on 14 November, saying he held her, kissed her cheek and touched her breasts despite her objections. Amnesty International Nigeria is calling on the Katsina State government and police to launch an immediate, transparent and independent investigation and to hold anyone found culpable to account, regardless of status.

stories.h: Overloaded boat capsize kills at least 24 Nigerians travelling to a funeral in Bayelsa
stories.e: An overcrowded boat suffered a mechanical failure and capsized while ferrying mourners from Ayama to Ukubie in Bayelsa State's Southern Ijaw area on Friday, with authorities confirming at least 24 dead and search efforts continuing; residents say as many as 300 people may have been on board. It is the latest in a string of deadly boat accidents on Nigeria's waterways this year, which campaigners link to recurring failures in enforcing overloading and vessel-safety rules.

stories.h: Tinubu approves N250 million for families as Bayelsa boat accident toll hits 29
stories.e: President Bola Tinubu has approved N250 million in support for the families of victims of a boat accident in Bayelsa State, as the confirmed death toll rose to 29. The tragedy is the latest in a long run of deadly waterway accidents across Nigerias riverine communities, which campaigners say points to a persistent failure to enforce boat safety regulations.

stories.h: Niger State government confirms bandit attack in Borgu killed five people
stories.e: Authorities in Niger State have confirmed that an attack by armed bandits on a community in the Borgu local government area left five people dead, amid a wider pattern of rural violence across the states north. The confirmation follows days of reports of killings in the area and comes as residents accuse security forces of being slow to respond.

stories.h: Gombe residents accuse Air Force personnel of shooting, beating civilians, killing three
stories.e: Residents of Lawanti community in Gombe State's Akko local government area allege that personnel from a Nigerian Air Force combat reconnaissance unit opened fire on and beat civilians following a dispute over suspected cable theft, leaving three people dead and thirteen injured, one critically. Governor Inuwa Yahaya has condemned the incident and ordered an investigation, while the Air Force has yet to respond publicly to the allegations.

stories.h: Deadly attack on Niger State villages triggers reprisal killings
stories.e: Suspected terrorists attacked the Lumman-Baare and Gada-Oli communities in Borgu council area of Niger State on Saturday morning, killing at least five people according to police, with other accounts putting the toll far higher. The assault, which saw a village head and his wife killed and his palace burnt, set off reprisal attacks against Fulani residents in nearby settlements including Wawa, amid weeks of rising intercommunal tension in the area. Police say joint security teams have been deployed and efforts to catch the attackers are ongoing.

stories.h: Deadly Niger State attack triggers ethnic reprisal killings in Borgu
stories.e: Suspected Boko Haram-linked gunmen killed at least 11 people, including a village head and his family, in a dawn raid on Lumman-Ba'are in Niger State's Borgu council area. The attack triggered reprisal killings by Kambari militias against Fulani residents in nearby towns, with eyewitnesses reporting around 20 bodies in Wawa alone.

stories.h: Nigerian Air Force personnel kill three, injure 13 in Gombe village shooting
stories.e: Three residents of Lawanti village in Gombe State's Akko council area died and 13 were injured after Nigerian Air Force personnel allegedly opened fire following a dispute over stolen cables at a military base. Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya has ordered an investigation and sent a delegation to the community to calm tensions.

stories.h: Akwa Ibom gender-based violence committee flags rise in teenage sextortion cases
stories.e: A lawyer leading Akwa Ibom States Gender-Based Violence Management Committee has warned of a growing pattern of sextortion targeting teenage girls, in which victims aged 13 to 19 are lured into sexual activity and then blackmailed using intimate images. The committee, which has recorded 340 gender-based violence cases in the state so far this year, said stigma and fear of retaliation mean many such cases go unreported.

stories.h: Eleven Malians remanded in Abuja over alleged kidnapping, trafficking
stories.e: A Federal High Court in Abuja remanded eleven Malian nationals, four of them women, after they pleaded not guilty to charges of detaining trafficking victims for ransom and trafficking persons for exploitation. Prosecutors allege the offences occurred in Abuja between March and April 2026, and the case was adjourned to January while the defence explores a possible plea bargain.

stories.h: Borno children demand stronger security and child-protection reforms
stories.e: Children at a World Children's Day forum in Maiduguri, organised by Plan International Nigeria, the Borno State government and the Joining Forces coalition, called on President Bola Tinubu and state authorities to improve school security and reform child-protection laws. Save the Children urged the state to update its Child Protection Law and make the Borno State Children's Parliament permanent, while UNICEF warned that aid meant for malnourished children was being diverted and sold. The event drew roughly 300 participants, including 200 children, under the theme "My day, my rights, my future."

stories.h: Over 50 feared dead as mourners' boat capsizes in Bayelsa
stories.e: A boat carrying mourners to a funeral capsized on the waterway between Oweikorogha and Angiama in Bayelsa State's Southern Ijaw area on Friday, with more than 50 bodies reportedly recovered and around 100 passengers still unaccounted for. Witnesses say the vessel was dangerously overloaded and that pleas to offload some passengers before continuing were ignored. Search and rescue efforts were ongoing as of Friday evening, and authorities had yet to confirm an official casualty figure.

stories.h: Former Super Eagles captain Odegbami survives armed attack at his home
stories.e: Former Nigeria national team captain Segun Odegbami says he survived an attack by three armed men who broke into his Abeokuta residence in the early hours of Friday, describing it as an assassination attempt. He said he and his household staff fought off the intruders, and he was treated in hospital and later discharged. Ogun State's police commissioner has ordered an investigation and launched a manhunt, though no motive has yet been established.

stories.h: Ukraine denies widening war with Russia after deadly strikes off Libyas coast
stories.e: Ukraines foreign minister has denied that Kyiv is expanding its war with Russia, after President Volodymyr Zelenskyy admitted Ukrainian forces struck a Russian warship and a cargo vessel off Libyas coast, killing an unspecified number of Libyan and Russian nationals. Libyas eastern government and a United Nations mission both condemned the attack as a breach of the countrys sovereignty, while Kyiv insisted its operations remain defensive and targeted only Russian military assets. The incident highlights Russias deepening military ties with factions in Libyas divided territory.

stories.h: South Africa court sets aside Phala Phala report, halting Ramaphosa impeachment bid
stories.e: South Africa's Western Cape High Court ruled on Wednesday that the independent Section 89 panel report on President Cyril Ramaphosa's Phala Phala farm scandal was unlawful and set it aside in full, finding the panel had misunderstood its own mandate. The ruling halts the parliamentary impeachment process built on that report, though an appeal is expected.

stories.h: Russia-Ukraine war reaches Africa as Zelenskyy claims ship attacks off Libya
stories.e: Ukraine says it used naval drones to sink a Russian corvette and strike a cargo vessel allegedly carrying weapons in Benghazi, Libya, marking a significant geographic expansion of the war. Libyan authorities and the UN mission in Libya have condemned the strikes and called for an independent investigation.

stories.h: Nigerian delegation skips COP31 closing plenary as summit ends without final deal
stories.e: COP31 closed in Antalya without parties approving the proposed outcome document, after talks ran nearly two days past schedule in the convention's longest-ever session. Nigeria's head of delegation and ministers did not attend or speak at the closing plenary, with officials saying the country's position had been conveyed through the African Group of Negotiators, leaving questions about transparency over its roughly 1,500-strong delegation.

stories.h: COP31 climate talks in Turkey end in deadlock after nearly 48-hour overrun
stories.e: UN climate negotiations in Turkey failed to produce a final agreement after talks ran almost two days past their scheduled close, with the EU, UK, Canada and Norway rejecting the presidencys draft text while African negotiators voiced frustration at the process. Officials warned the impasse, only the second of its kind in the conventions history, could delay progress on fossil-fuel phase-out and climate finance pledges that matter directly to Nigerias own funding ambitions.

stories.h: Civil society groups warn COP31 climate talks risk a disappointing outcome
stories.e: A coalition of 100 civil society groups, including Nigeria's Environmental Rights Action, HOMEF and Parents for Future Nigeria, has accused the COP31 presidencies of Türkiye and Australia of weak leadership as climate talks in Antalya ran past their scheduled close. The groups criticised the removal of explicit fossil fuel transition language and a dropped $120 billion annual adaptation finance target.

stories.h: Nearly 600 women killed in South Africa in just three months
stories.e: South African police said 581 women were killed between July and September 2026, including 13 whose bodies were dumped in public spaces in Ekurhuleni and a separate attack in Botshabelo that killed five women and a toddler. Police Minister Firoz Cachalia called for greater efforts to protect women and children from violence, as the country continues to record one of the world's highest femicide rates.

stories.h: African Union launches continental credit rating agency to challenge global assessments
stories.e: The African Union has launched the Africa Credit Rating Agency, based in Mauritius, aiming to assess African governments and companies using local data and expertise rather than relying solely on global agencies. Interim chief executive Sifiso Falala says the agency is in talks with fifteen governments and expects to issue its first sovereign ratings by the end of March, arguing that subjective assessments have cost African nations tens of billions of dollars in higher borrowing costs. Analysts caution its credibility will hinge on maintaining independence, since governments pay for its sovereign ratings.

stories.h: China, US and Russia issue joint 'Declaration Toward Peace' after historic summit
stories.e: Presidents Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin held an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China, after which the three powers issued a joint statement setting out shared ambitions to reform the United Nations and curb the reach of the International Criminal Court. European leaders including Germany's Friedrich Merz and France's Emmanuel Macron were dismissive of the talks, even as Trump and Putin both described the meeting as historic.

stories.h: Ghana's public debt jumps 32% to $65.3 billion under Mahama
stories.e: Ghana's public debt has risen by 32 per cent to $65.3 billion in under two years under President John Mahama's administration, according to new figures. The sharp increase raises questions about fiscal management in one of West Africa's largest economies, with implications for regional economic stability.

stories.h: Activist warns COP31 carbon removal push could hurt African farmland and fisheries
stories.e: Kwami Kpondzo of the Global Forest Coalition has warned that carbon dioxide removal technologies being pushed at the COP31 climate talks could worsen food insecurity and strain African smallholder farmers and fishing communities. He argued that large-scale bioenergy and ocean-based removal schemes let big polluters avoid cutting emissions at source, and that climate finance should not be diverted from adaptation support that developing nations, including Nigeria, are owed.

stories.h: Nigeria reviews report on diplomatic row with South Africa over livestream
stories.e: Nigeria's foreign ministry says it is reviewing a report on a diplomatic spat after its High Commissioner to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, accused Pretoria of cutting the livestream of his credentials speech, a claim South African officials deny. Pretoria summoned Fani-Kayode over the public complaint, which it says breached diplomatic protocol, straining relations between the two African countries.

stories.h: Eight Nigerians among twelve arrested in Canada over $4.5m car theft ring
stories.e: Police in Ontario, Canada, arrested eight Nigerians and four others accused of running a syndicate that stole and disguised high-value vehicles for export to West Africa. Investigators recovered 96 vehicles worth about $4.5 million hidden in shipping containers, and the suspects face 231 charges in total.

stories.h: South Africa summons Nigerian envoy over livestream row
stories.e: South Africa's foreign ministry summoned Nigeria's High Commissioner, Femi Fani-Kayode, accusing him of breaching diplomatic protocol after he publicly alleged that his credential-presentation speech had been deliberately cut from the presidential livestream. South African officials and the public broadcaster rejected the claim, and both sides later described their meeting as cordial, even as the incident added fresh strain to relations already tense since deadly anti-Nigerian violence in April.

stories.h: COP31: Observers raise concerns as presidencies publish first draft of cover decision
stories.e: Civil society observers at the COP31 climate summit have criticised the first draft of the conference's cover decision, arguing it falls short on ambition for emissions cuts and climate finance. The concerns echo long-standing complaints from African delegations, including Nigeria's, that wealthier nations are not matching their climate pledges with adequate funding.

stories.h: Seventeen killed in separate overnight shootings across South Africa
stories.e: Seventeen people were shot dead in two unconnected incidents in South Africa on Sunday night, eight men killed inside a minibus in KwaZulu-Natal and nine others, including three women, shot inside a shack near Pretoria. Police say no suspects have been identified and have launched manhunts, as the country continues to grapple with gun violence that claimed nearly 5,500 lives between April and June alone.

stories.h: Nigeria's mission in South Africa urges calm after row over Ramaphosa spokesman's remarks
stories.e: Nigeria's High Commission in South Africa has called for restraint after President Cyril Ramaphosa's spokesperson accused Nigerian envoy Femi Fani-Kayode of lying about Ramaphosa's intervention in a dispute over a disrupted livestream of his credentialing ceremony. The Nigerian mission said the matter should be handled through diplomatic channels and declared the issue closed, while warning it was ready to respond further if South Africa chose to escalate.

stories.h: Ebola cases in DR Congo surpass 11,000 as insecurity hampers response
stories.e: The World Health Organisation says confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo have passed 11,000, with over 5,400 deaths, as armed attacks on health facilities and workers continue to disrupt containment efforts. Nigeria's own imported case has recovered and all 62 traced contacts completed monitoring without further infection, though the NCDC cautions the outbreak is not yet officially over.

stories.h: AfDB and Japan's JICA sign $583 million deal to fund Africa's poorest countries
stories.e: The African Development Bank and the Japan International Cooperation Agency have signed a concessional loan agreement worth roughly $583 million to support the African Development Fund's seventeenth replenishment. Signed in Tokyo by AfDB president Sidi Ould Tah and JICA president Akihiko Tanaka, it is described as Japan's largest-ever assistance package to the Fund, aimed at infrastructure, energy access and food security in low-income African states. The replenishment round overall raised a record $11 billion from 44 partners.

stories.h: Cabo Verde votes as incumbent president seeks second term
stories.e: Cabo Verdeans went to the polls to elect a president, with incumbent José Maria Neves, who took office in 2021, seeking a second term against several challengers including Joana Rosa of the opposition MpD. A runoff is scheduled for 29 November if no candidate wins an outright majority in the first round.

stories.h: CAS overturns CAF ruling, restores Senegals 2025 AFCON title after Morocco final dispute
stories.e: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled in Senegals favour, overturning a CAF decision that had stripped the country of its 2025 AFCON title and ordering officials to immediately restore Senegals extra-time win over Morocco. CAF had earlier awarded Morocco the trophy after Senegalese players briefly walked off the pitch during stoppage time in the January final, but CAS found in the Senegalese federations favour and directed CAF to correct its official records. The ruling settles months of dispute between the two football federations over one of the continents most prestigious titles.

stories.h: FIFA confirms joint US bid to host 2031 Women's World Cup, UK to stage 2035 edition
stories.e: FIFA has confirmed that a joint United States bid will host the 2031 Women's World Cup, with the United Kingdom set to stage the following edition in 2035. The decision continues football's recent pattern of awarding major women's tournaments years in advance to give host nations more time to prepare.

stories.h: Court of Arbitration for Sport to rule Tuesday on Senegal's AFCON title appeal
stories.e: The Court of Arbitration for Sport has scheduled Tuesday for its verdict on Senegal's appeal relating to their Africa Cup of Nations title. The ruling is being closely watched across the continent given its implications for the tournament's outcome and Senegal's standing as reigning champions.

stories.h: Alex Iwobi becomes first African to make 100 Premier League starts for Fulham
stories.e: Nigerian midfielder Alex Iwobi became the first African player to reach 100 Premier League starts for Fulham, achieving the milestone during Fulham's 1-1 draw with Manchester City. In a separate match, compatriot Taiwo Awoniyi opened the scoring for Coventry City in their 3-2 win over bottom-placed Crystal Palace, before going off with an ankle injury of unclear severity.

stories.h: CAF returns to profit as Motsepe-era reforms reshape its finances
stories.e: African footballs governing body posted a 31.2 million dollar net profit for the financial year to June, alongside revenue of 284 million dollars, as it presented its latest accounts at its general assembly in Abuja. CAF said its reserves have swung from a 16.8 million dollar deficit into positive territory, and it has also sharply increased payouts to member associations and clubs, including higher prize money for both the mens and womens continental cups. The Abuja meeting marked the first time in seventeen years Nigeria has hosted the assembly.

stories.h: CAF approves new U-17 womens tournament, opens bidding for WAFCON 2028
stories.e: Meeting in Abuja, CAFs executive committee approved a new Under-17 Womens Africa Cup of Nations aimed at developing young female talent across the continent, and opened bidding for hosting rights to the 2028 Womens Africa Cup of Nations. Member federations have three weeks to submit bids for the 2028 tournament, which is planned for March and April with qualifiers starting the following year. The committee also discussed plans to improve refereeing standards through a new elite referees programme.

stories.h: FIFA president praises Delta State's Warri Stadium remodelling
stories.e: FIFA President Gianni Infantino commended Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori for investing in the remodelling of Warri City Stadium, calling modern sporting infrastructure essential for developing football talent. He also inaugurated the Hussey College Sports Complex in Warri during the visit and praised Nigeria's recent U-17 women's World Cup performance.

stories.h: African football body backs Infantino for fourth FIFA term at Abuja assembly
stories.e: CAF President Patrice Motsepe told the confederations general assembly in Abuja that all 54 African member associations unanimously back Gianni Infantinos bid for a fourth term as FIFA president, ahead of a vote scheduled for March 2027 in Rabat. Infantino, who has already secured South American backing but lost European support, has pledged 25 million dollars to each CAF member for development projects from January 2027.

stories.h: FIFA president Infantino set to commission reconstructed Warri stadium
stories.e: FIFA President Gianni Infantino is expected in Delta State to officially commission the newly reconstructed Warri City Stadium, pledging continued FIFA support for Nigerian football. The visit marks a milestone for the state governments multi-year effort to upgrade the stadiums pitch, tracks and facilities to international standards.

stories.h: FIFA president Infantino visits Warri, pledges support for Nigerian football
stories.e: FIFA president Gianni Infantino visited Warri in Delta State ahead of the unveiling of the newly reconstructed Warri City Stadium, praising the state's investment in grassroots football. Governor Sheriff Oborevwori's administration rebuilt the stadium, which officials say is intended to boost football development across the Niger Delta.

stories.h: FIFA president Infantino tours renovated Warri City Stadium ahead of commissioning
stories.e: FIFA president Gianni Infantino visited Delta State to inspect the newly rebuilt Warri City Stadium ahead of its formal commissioning, which is expected to be attended by CAF president Patrice Motsepe. Infantino praised the facility and argued that developing smaller, community-level stadiums matters as much to footballs growth as hosting major tournaments, as part of Delta States wider investment in sporting infrastructure.

stories.h: CAF unveils official logo for 2027 Africa Cup of Nations
stories.e: The Confederation of African Football and host nations Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda have jointly unveiled the official emblem for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, simultaneously launched in all three countries. The design, built around a traditional East African shield with the tournament trophy at its centre, is meant to represent the shared heritage and identity of the three co-hosts ahead of the continental tournament.

stories.h: National Sports Commission postpones Enugu 2026 festival to May 2027
stories.e: Nigeria's National Sports Commission has approved postponing the Enugu 2026 National Sports Festival to May 2027. The Local Organising Committee cited circumstances beyond the Enugu State Government's control, delaying one of the country's major multi-sport events.

stories.h: FIFA appoints five-member Normalisation Committee to run NFF until May 2027
stories.e: FIFA has installed a five-member Normalisation Committee, chaired by former League Management Company lawyer Samson Ebomhe and including ex-international Daniel Amokachi, to run the Nigeria Football Federation's affairs with immediate effect. The committee, which also features Godwin Enakhena, Joe Abah and Amina Yerima, must review the NFF's statutes and electoral code, push wider stakeholder representation, and oversee fresh leadership elections before its mandate ends in May 2027. Members are barred from contesting those elections themselves, and the outgoing NFF administration has been told to cooperate fully with the takeover.

stories.h: CAF president Motsepe arrives in Abuja for general assembly
stories.e: CAF president Patrice Motsepe arrived in Abuja ahead of the 48th CAF Ordinary General Assembly, which Nigeria is hosting for the first time in 17 years. The gathering brings together officials from CAF's 54 member associations, alongside the FIFA president, days before Nigeria also hosts the CAF Awards in Lagos.

stories.h: Super Eagles climb to 29th in FIFA world rankings, fifth in Africa
stories.e: Nigeria's Super Eagles rose one place to 29th in the latest FIFA world rankings, moving above Algeria into fifth place in Africa, after a 3-1 win over Tanzania was followed by a goalless draw in the reverse fixture. The gain reflects Algeria's decline as much as Nigeria's own form, with coach Eric Chelle still working to find consistency ahead of the 2027 AFCON qualifiers.

stories.h: Super Eagles held to goalless draw by Tanzania in AFCON qualifying setback
stories.e: Nigeria's Super Eagles were held 0-0 by Tanzania's Taifa Stars in Zanzibar, missing the chance to build on their first-leg win in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers. Coach Eric Chelle's side struggled to convert chances despite periods of control, leaving work to do in the remaining qualifying fixtures.

stories.h: Super Eagles held to goalless draw by Tanzania in AFCON qualifier
stories.e: Nigeria’s Super Eagles were held to a 0-0 draw by Tanzania in Zanzibar in their latest 2027 AFCON qualifying fixture, despite having won the reverse leg 3-1 in Uyo. The result leaves Nigeria level on seven points with Guinea-Bissau at the top of Group L, with only the group winner guaranteed a place at the finals. The draw raises pressure on the team to improve its finishing in the remaining qualifiers.

stories.h: Abia dissolves Enyimba management amid relegation battle
stories.e: The Abia State Government has dissolved Enyimba International's management and technical crew after the storied club slipped to 18th place in the Nigeria Premier Football League following 13 matches. Officials cited administrative and structural problems and said the Ministry of Sports and Youth Development would take over running the club while a restructuring plan is worked out.

stories.h: Tanzania hold Super Eagles to goalless draw in AFCON qualifier
stories.e: Nigeria's Super Eagles were held 0-0 by Tanzania in Zanzibar in their 2027 AFCON qualifying return leg, missing several chances including a crossbar strike from Tolu Arokodare. The draw leaves Nigeria level on points with Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau, and under pressure to improve their finishing with qualification for the tournament still not secured.
